title: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
parties: Shreya Singhal vs Union of India
summary: Struck down Section 66A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 in its entirety for violating Article 19(1)(a). Held that liberty of thought and expression cannot be suppressed on vague assertions of causing annoyance or inconvenience.

title: Arjun Panditrao Khotkar v. Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal
judge: R.F. Nariman, S. Ravindra Bhat, V. Ramasubramanian
parties: Arjun Panditrao Khotkar vs Kailash Kushanrao Gorantyal
summary: Settled conflicting precedents by ruling that a certificate under Section 65B(4) is an absolute condition precedent for the admissibility of electronic records as secondary evidence in legal proceedings.

title: Anvar P.V. v. P.K. Basheer
judge: R.M. Lodha, Kurian Joseph, R.F. Nariman
parties: Anvar P.V. vs P.K. Basheer
summary: Overruled Navjot Sandhu on electronic evidence, holding that Sections 65A and 65B constitute a complete code and electronic records cannot be proved by general oral evidence.

title: Avnish Bajaj v. State (NCT of Delhi)
parties: Avnish Bajaj (Bazee.com) vs State
summary: Addressed intermediary liability for user-generated content hosted on an e-commerce platform, prompting the subsequent amendment of Section 79 to introduce the safe harbor doctrine.

title: Internet and Mobile Association of India v. Reserve Bank of India
judge: R.F. Nariman, Aniruddha Bose, V. Ramasubramanian
parties: IAMAI vs Reserve Bank of India
summary: Set aside the RBI circular banning banks from providing services to virtual currency exchanges, ruling that the blanket ban failed the constitutional proportionality test under Article 19(1)(g).

title: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India
judge: J.S. Khehar, J. Chelameswar, S.A. Bobde, D.Y. Chandrachud, et al.
parties: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy vs Union of India
summary: Nine-judge constitution bench unanimously held that privacy is a fundamental right emanating from Article 21, establishing the requirements of legality, legitimate aim, and proportionality for state infringement.

title: Anuradha Bhasin v. Union of India
judge: N.V. Ramana, R. Subhash Reddy, B.R. Gavai
parties: Anuradha Bhasin vs Union of India
summary: Held that access to the internet is constitutionally protected under Article 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(g). Indefinite internet suspensions are impermissible and must comply with proportionality and periodic review.

title: State of Tamil Nadu v. Cyber Phishing Syndicate
parties: State vs Cyber Phishing Accused
summary: Affirmed the framing of charges under Sections 66C and 66D of the IT Act along with Section 420 IPC for orchestrating fraudulent spoofed banking portals to harvest login credentials.

title: Google LLC v. Competition Commission of India
parties: Google LLC vs Competition Commission of India
summary: Upheld major competition findings regarding dominant position abuse in the mobile operating system market, underscoring anti-trust regulations in digital platform ecosystems.

title: Foundation for Independent Journalism v. Union of India
parties: Foundation for Independent Journalism vs Union of India
summary: Examined the constitutional validity of Part III of the Information Technology (Intermediary Guidelines and Digital Media Ethics Code) Rules, 2021 regarding digital news publishers.

title: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
judge: Chandramauli Kr. Prasad, Pinaki Chandra Ghose
parties: Arnesh Kumar vs State of Bihar & Anr
summary: Formulated mandatory directives prohibiting automatic arrests for offences punishable with imprisonment of seven years or less without recording specific reasons under Section 41 CrPC.

title: Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation
parties: Satender Kumar Antil vs CBI
summary: Issued comprehensive landmark guidelines categorizing offences into groups A, B, C, and D to prevent unnecessary pre-trial detention and ensure consistent bail adjudication.

title: Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation
parties: Sanjay Chandra vs CBI
summary: Reaffirmed that the primary purpose of bail is securing attendance at trial, not pre-conviction punishment, even in complex corporate and economic cases.

title: Dataram Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
parties: Dataram Singh vs State of Uttar Pradesh
summary: Held that a fundamental postulate of criminal jurisprudence is the presumption of innocence; denying bail unnecessarily infringes fundamental liberties.

title: Babu Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
parties: Babu Singh vs State of U.P.
summary: Established that an earlier rejection of a bail application does not operate as res judicata when circumstances change or trial faces unreasonable delays.

title: Sushila Aggarwal v. State (NCT of Delhi)
judge: Arun Mishra, Indira Banerjee, Vineet Saran, M.R. Shah, S. Ravindra Bhat
parties: Sushila Aggarwal vs State (NCT of Delhi)
summary: Constitution bench held that anticipatory bail under Section 438 CrPC should not be invariably limited to a fixed time period and can continue until the conclusion of the trial.

title: P. Chidambaram v. Directorate of Enforcement
judge: R. Banumathi, A.S. Bopanna, Hrishikesh Roy
parties: P. Chidambaram vs Enforcement Directorate
summary: Emphasized that bail considerations turn on the triple test: whether the accused is a flight risk, likely to tamper with evidence, or likely to influence witnesses.

title: D.K. Basu v. State of West Bengal
parties: D.K. Basu vs State of West Bengal
summary: Laid down mandatory guidelines for law enforcement during arrest and interrogation to eliminate custodial deaths and uphold constitutional guarantees under Articles 21 and 22.

title: Lalita Kumari v. Government of Uttar Pradesh
judge: P. Sathasivam, B.S. Chauhan, Ranjana P. Desai, Ranjan Gogoi, S.A. Bobde
parties: Lalita Kumari vs Govt. of U.P.
summary: Held that registration of an FIR under Section 154 CrPC is mandatory if the information discloses the commission of a cognizable offence, without room for preliminary inquiry except in narrow exceptions.

title: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal
judge: S. Ratnavel Pandian, K. Jayachandra Reddy
parties: State of Haryana vs Bhajan Lal
summary: Formulated the foundational seven illustrative categories governing when High Courts can exercise inherent powers under Section 482 CrPC to quash malicious or legally untenable FIRs.

title: Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. v. State of Maharashtra
judge: D.Y. Chandrachud, M.R. Shah, Sanjiv Khanna
parties: Neeharika Infrastructure vs State of Maharashtra
summary: Held that High Courts should not pass blanket orders restraining arrest or investigation during Section 482 petitions except in extraordinary and rarest of rare cases.

title: Md. Asfak Alam v. State of Jharkhand
parties: Md. Asfak Alam vs State of Jharkhand
summary: Strictly directed courts and police forces nationwide to enforce Arnesh Kumar guidelines and penalize officers engaging in unlawful or mechanical arrests.

title: Aman Preet Singh v. C.B.I.
parties: Aman Preet Singh vs CBI
summary: Held that trial courts cannot mechanically insist on remanding an accused to custody merely because a chargesheet has been submitted under Section 170 CrPC if they cooperated throughout investigation.

title: Manish Sisodia v. Directorate of Enforcement
parties: Manish Sisodia vs Enforcement Directorate
summary: Ruled that where an accused has suffered prolonged custody and trial delay without fault, constitutional liberty under Article 21 takes precedence over statutory bail restrictions under Section 45 PMLA.

title: Prem Prakash v. Union of India
parties: Prem Prakash vs Union of India
summary: Clarified the evidentiary admissibility of statements recorded under Section 50 PMLA, affirming that statements procured while in police or judicial custody remain vulnerable to evidentiary exclusions.

title: State of Kerala v. Rajesh
parties: State of Kerala vs Rajesh
act_tags: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
summary: Reiterated strict compliance with twin conditions under Section 37 NDPS before granting bail for commercial contraband, requiring satisfaction that accused is not guilty and unlikely to reoffend.

title: Mohd Muslim @ Hussain v. State (NCT of Delhi)
parties: Mohd Muslim vs State (NCT of Delhi)
act_tags: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
summary: Held that systemic delay in trial and prolonged incarceration of undertrials under the NDPS Act can supersede statutory limits of Section 37 to uphold Article 21.

title: Toofan Singh v. State of Tamil Nadu
judge: R.F. Nariman, Navin Sinha, Indira Banerjee
parties: Toofan Singh vs State of Tamil Nadu
act_tags: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
summary: Three-judge bench held that officers designated under Section 53 NDPS are police officers; therefore, confessional statements recorded under Section 67 cannot be utilized as substantive evidence.

title: Sanjeev Chandra Agarwal v. Union of India
parties: Sanjeev Chandra Agarwal vs Union of India
act_tags: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
summary: Analyzed Section 27A NDPS regarding financing illicit drug trafficking, demanding tangible documentary or financial evidence rather than conjecture to invoke severe statutory bars.

title: Gurdev Singh v. State of Punjab
parties: Gurdev Singh vs State of Punjab
act_tags: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
summary: Held that while awarding sentence under the NDPS Act, courts must account for quantity recovered, past criminal record, and age of the accused.

title: Hira Singh v. Union of India
judge: Arun Mishra, Indira Banerjee, M.R. Shah
parties: Hira Singh vs Union of India
act_tags: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
summary: Held that in mixture of narcotic drug and neutral substance, total weight of mixture is to be considered, not just pure drug content, to determine commercial quantity.

title: Vijaysinh Chandubha Jadeja v. State of Gujarat
judge: D.K. Jain, P. Sathasivam, J.M. Panchal, R.M. Lodha, H.L. Dattu
parties: Vijaysinh Chandubha Jadeja vs State of Gujarat
act_tags: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
summary: Constitution bench held that informing suspect of their statutory right under Section 50 NDPS to be searched before a Gazetted Officer or Magistrate is mandatory; failure vitiates conviction.

title: Rabi Prakash v. State of Odisha
parties: Rabi Prakash vs State of Odisha
act_tags: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
summary: Affirmed that fundamental right to a speedy trial under Article 21 applies to offences under special statutes including Section 37 NDPS.

title: State by (NCB) Bengaluru v. Pallulabid Ahmad Arimutta
judge: N.V. Ramana, A.S. Bopanna, Hima Kohli
parties: NCB vs Pallulabid Ahmad Arimutta
act_tags: Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985
summary: Held that statements of co-accused recorded under Section 67 NDPS and voluntary disclosure statements cannot form the sole foundation to reject bail.

title: Union of India v. K.A. Najeeb
judge: N.V. Ramana, Surya Kant, Aniruddha Bose
parties: Union of India vs K.A. Najeeb
summary: Held that statutory bars on bail in special penal statutes (UAPA/NDPS) do not curtail the constitutional powers of High Courts and the Supreme Court under Article 21 where trial is protracted.

title: APS Forex Services Pvt. Ltd. v. Shakti International Fashion Linkers
parties: APS Forex Services vs Shakti International
summary: Held that once issuance of cheque and signature are admitted, there is a strong statutory presumption that cheque was issued in discharge of a legally enforceable debt.

title: Kishan Rao v. Shankargouda
parties: Kishan Rao vs Shankargouda
summary: Affirmed that the accused may rebut presumption under Section 139 NI Act through preponderance of probabilities, but a mere bald denial of liability is insufficient.

title: Rangappa v. Sri Mohan
judge: K.G. Balakrishnan, P. Sathasivam, J.M. Panchal
parties: Rangappa vs Sri Mohan
summary: Three-judge bench held that the presumption mandated by Section 139 NI Act indeed includes the existence of a legally enforceable debt.

title: M/s Gimpex Private Limited v. Manoj Goel
parties: Gimpex Pvt. Ltd. vs Manoj Goel
summary: Held that when parties enter into a settlement agreement compromising Section 138 proceedings, default under the settlement agreement gives rise to a fresh cause of action.

title: Sunil Todi v. State of Gujarat
parties: Sunil Todi vs State of Gujarat
summary: Held that a cheque issued as a security deposit or advance against an underlying contract falls under Section 138 if debt has become legally enforceable by the date of presentment.

title: Kalamani Tex v. P. Balasubramanian
judge: N.V. Ramana, Surya Kant, Aniruddha Bose
parties: Kalamani Tex vs P. Balasubramanian
summary: Held that even if a blank signed cheque leaf is voluntarily handed over, the drawer gives implied authority to holder to fill details, attracting the presumption under Section 139.

title: Alka Khandu Avhad v. Amar Syamprasad Mishra
parties: Alka Khandu Avhad vs Amar Syamprasad Mishra
summary: Held that a joint account holder who is not a signatory to the dishonoured cheque cannot be prosecuted under Section 138 unless vicarious liability applies under Section 141.

title: Bir Singh v. Mukesh Kumar
parties: Bir Singh vs Mukesh Kumar
summary: Reiterated that signature on the cheque being undisputed triggers the statutory presumption in favor of the payee, irrespective of who filled the contents.

title: Dashrathbhai Trikambhai Patel v. Hitesh Mahendrabhai Patel
parties: Dashrathbhai Patel vs Hitesh Patel
summary: Held that where part-payment has been made before presentation, failure to endorse part-payment on cheque under Section 56 prevents Section 138 from being triggered for original full amount.

title: Yogesh Jain v. Sumesh Chadha
parties: Yogesh Jain vs Sumesh Chadha
summary: Held that grant of interim compensation under Section 143A NI Act is discretionary and not mandatory; trial court must apply judicial mind and record reasons.

title: Vidya Drolia v. Durga Trading Corporation
judge: N.V. Ramana, Sanjiv Khanna, Krishna Murari
parties: Vidya Drolia vs Durga Trading Corporation
summary: Laid down the definitive four-fold test to determine when subject matter of a dispute is non-arbitrable, overruling earlier precedents on landlord-tenant matters.

title: In Re: Interplay Between Arbitration Agreements and Stamp Act
judge: D.Y. Chandrachud, S.K. Kaul, Sanjiv Khanna, B.R. Gavai, Surya Kant, et al.
parties: Curative Bench Seven Judges
summary: Seven-judge bench unanimously held that non-stamping or insufficient stamping of an underlying commercial contract does not render the arbitration clause void ab initio at referral stage.

title: Energy Watchdog v. Central Electricity Regulatory Commission
parties: Energy Watchdog vs CERC & Ors
summary: Held that unexpected rise in raw material or import prices causing commercial hardship does not constitute frustration of contract under Section 56.

title: Halliburton Offshore Services Inc. v. Vedanta Limited
parties: Halliburton Offshore vs Vedanta Ltd
summary: Held that Covid-19 pandemic cannot be used as an automatic excuse to escape contractual performance or restrain invocation of unconditional bank guarantees.

title: Amazon.com NV Investment Holdings LLC v. Future Retail Ltd.
parties: Amazon.com NV vs Future Retail Ltd
summary: Held that interim orders passed by an Emergency Arbitrator under institutional arbitration rules are enforceable in Indian courts under Section 17(2).

title: Associate Builders v. Delhi Development Authority
parties: Associate Builders vs DDA
summary: Defined parameters of 'public policy of India' under Section 34, holding that merits of an arbitral award cannot be reopened unless award shocks the conscience of court.

title: Ssangyong Engineering & Construction Co. Ltd. v. NHAI
parties: Ssangyong Engineering vs NHAI
summary: Clarified post-2015 amendment scope of Section 34, ruling that mere misconstruction of a contract does not justify setting aside an award unless interpretation is impossible.

title: Novartis AG v. Union of India
parties: Novartis AG vs Union of India
summary: Denied patent for beta crystalline form of Imatinib Mesylate, upholding Section 3(d) as valid safeguard against evergreening of pharmaceutical patents.

title: Bajaj Auto Ltd. v. TVS Motor Company Ltd.
parties: Bajaj Auto vs TVS Motor Co
summary: Directed trial courts to hear patent infringement suits on a day-to-day basis and resolve matters within four months without lingering on interlocutory stages.

title: The Chancellor, Masters & Scholars of University of Oxford v. Rameshwari Photocopy Services
parties: Oxford University Press vs Rameshwari Photocopy
summary: Held that creation of course packs by photocopiers for students is protected under Section 52(1)(i) of the Copyright Act as fair use for educational instruction.

title: Renaissance Hotel Holdings Inc. v. B. Vijaya Sai
judge: L. Nageswara Rao, B.R. Gavai, B.V. Nagarathna
parties: Renaissance Hotel vs B. Vijaya Sai
summary: Held that once a registered trademark is used identically in relation to identical goods or services, trademark infringement is established under Section 29 without requiring proof of actual confusion.

title: N.N. Global Mercantile Pvt. Ltd. v. Indo Unique Flame Ltd.
judge: K.M. Joseph, Ajay Rastogi, Aniruddha Bose, Hrishikesh Roy, C.T. Ravikumar
parties: N.N. Global vs Indo Unique Flame
summary: Historical ruling on unstamped arbitration clauses which held such agreements unenforceable, subsequently overruled by the unanimous 7-judge curative bench in December 2023.

title: Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. v. Raman Ispat Pvt. Ltd.
parties: PVVNL vs Raman Ispat Pvt Ltd
summary: Held that Section 53 waterfall mechanism under IBC prevails over recovery provisions under the Electricity Act, confirming the non-obstante priority of IBC under Section 238.

title: Swiss Ribbons Pvt. Ltd. v. Union of India
parties: Swiss Ribbons vs Union of India
summary: Upheld constitutional validity of Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, affirming distinction between financial and operational creditors and primacy of resolution over recovery.

title: Committee of Creditors of Essar Steel India Ltd. v. Satish Kumar Gupta
judge: R.F. Nariman, Surya Kant, V. Ramasubramanian
parties: CoC Essar Steel vs Satish Kumar Gupta
summary: Reiterated primacy of commercial wisdom of the Committee of Creditors, limiting NCLT/NCLAT jurisdiction to procedural review without substituting business judgment.

title: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala
judge: S.M. Sikri, J.M. Shelat, K.S. Hegde, A.N. Grover, et al. (13-Judge Bench)
parties: Kesavananda Bharati vs State of Kerala
summary: Thirteen-judge bench formulated the Basic Structure Doctrine, establishing that Parliament's constituent power to amend the Constitution cannot alter or destroy its basic features.

title: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
judge: M.H. Beg, Y.V. Chandrachud, P.N. Bhagwati, V.R. Krishna Iyer, et al.
parties: Maneka Gandhi vs Union of India
summary: Expanded Article 21, establishing that procedure depriving liberty must be 'just, fair, and reasonable', linking Articles 14, 19, and 21 as the interlocked Golden Triangle.

title: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
judge: Dipak Misra, R.F. Nariman, A.M. Khanwilkar, D.Y. Chandrachud, Indu Malhotra
parties: Navtej Singh Johar vs Union of India
summary: Unanimously read down Section 377 IPC to decriminalize consensual same-sex relations between adults, holding that discrimination based on sexual orientation violates constitutional guarantees.

title: Joseph Shine v. Union of India
judge: Dipak Misra, R.F. Nariman, A.M. Khanwilkar, D.Y. Chandrachud, Indu Malhotra
parties: Joseph Shine vs Union of India
summary: Struck down Section 497 IPC criminalizing adultery as unconstitutional, ruling that treat women as chattel of their husbands violates Articles 14 and 21.

title: Shayara Bano v. Union of India
judge: J.S. Khehar, Kurian Joseph, R.F. Nariman, U.U. Lalit, S. Abdul Nazeer
parties: Shayara Bano vs Union of India
summary: By a 3:2 majority, held instantaneous Triple Talaq (Talaq-e-Biddat) void and unconstitutional, establishing the doctrine of manifest arbitrariness under Article 14.

title: Indian Young Lawyers Association v. State of Kerala
judge: Dipak Misra, R.F. Nariman, A.M. Khanwilkar, D.Y. Chandrachud, Indu Malhotra
parties: Indian Young Lawyers Association vs State of Kerala
act_tags: Kerala Hindu Places of Public Worship Rules, 1965
summary: Held custom barring entry of women aged 10-50 into Sabarimala temple unconstitutional, ruling religious freedom cannot override basic human dignity and gender equality.

title: Common Cause (A Regd. Society) v. Union of India
judge: Dipak Misra, A.K. Sikri, A.M. Khanwilkar, D.Y. Chandrachud, Ashok Bhushan
parties: Common Cause vs Union of India
summary: Recognized right to die with dignity as part of Article 21, validating living wills and passive euthanasia for terminally ill patients in permanent vegetative states.

title: National Legal Services Authority (NALSA) v. Union of India
parties: NALSA vs Union of India
summary: Recognized transgender persons as a third gender under the Constitution, upholding self-determination of gender identity as an integral part of personal liberty.

title: Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India (Electoral Bonds)
judge: D.Y. Chandrachud, Sanjiv Khanna, B.R. Gavai, J.B. Pardiwala, Manoj Misra
parties: ADR vs Union of India
summary: Constitution bench struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme as unconstitutional under Article 19(1)(a), holding that voters have a fundamental right to know political contributors.

title: Supriyo @ Supriya Chakraborty v. Union of India
judge: D.Y. Chandrachud, S.K. Kaul, S. Ravindra Bhat, Hima Kohli, P.S. Narasimha
parties: Supriyo vs Union of India
summary: Held that there is no unqualified fundamental right to marry, leaving the legal recognition of marriage for queer couples to the competence of Parliament.

title: K.S. Puttaswamy (Aadhaar-5J.) v. Union of India
judge: Dipak Misra, A.K. Sikri, A.M. Khanwilkar, D.Y. Chandrachud, Ashok Bhushan
parties: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy vs Union of India
summary: Upheld constitutional validity of Aadhaar for government welfare subsidies under Section 7, but struck down Section 57 permitting private corporate entities from demanding Aadhaar data.

title: People's Union for Civil Liberties (PUCL) v. Union of India (NOTA)
judge: P. Sathasivam, Ranjana P. Desai, Ranjan Gogoi
parties: PUCL vs Union of India
summary: Directed Election Commission to provide a 'None of the Above' (NOTA) button on electronic voting machines, empowering voters to express disapproval of all candidates.

title: Teesta Atul Setalvad v. State of Gujarat
judge: B.R. Gavai, A.S. Bopanna, Dipankar Datta
parties: Teesta Atul Setalvad vs State of Gujarat
summary: Three-judge bench granted regular bail, applying the beneficial proviso under Section 437(1) CrPC in favor of a woman accused, highlighting that continued detention was unwarranted.

title: Swaraj Abhiyan v. Union of India
parties: Swaraj Abhiyan vs Union of India
summary: Issued binding directives for drought management and social security implementation, holding that the right to food is an inseparable entitlement under Article 21.

title: T.N. Godavarman Thirumulpad v. Union of India
parties: T.N. Godavarman vs Union of India
summary: Established landmark continuing mandamus defining forests by dictionary meaning across India, restricting non-forest activities without central environmental clearance.

title: Newtech Promoters and Developers Pvt. Ltd. v. State of UP
judge: U.U. Lalit, Ajay Rastogi, Aniruddha Bose
parties: Newtech Promoters vs State of UP
summary: Affirmed that RERA applies retroactively to ongoing real estate projects initiated before the Act, protecting homebuyers' statutory rights to refunds with interest.

title: Pioneer Urban Land and Infrastructure Ltd. v. Govindan Raghavan
parties: Pioneer Urban Land vs Govindan Raghavan
summary: Held that builder-buyer agreements containing one-sided and unfair conditions cannot be enforced against homebuyers, constituting an unfair trade practice.

title: Wg. Cdr. Arifur Rahman Khan v. DLF Southern Homes Pvt. Ltd.
parties: Arifur Rahman Khan vs DLF Southern Homes
summary: Awarded compensation to flat buyers for delayed possession even after accepting conveyance deeds, holding that consumer rights survive physical handover.

title: Bikram Chatterjee v. Union of India (Amrapali Group)
parties: Bikram Chatterjee vs Union of India
summary: Exercised Article 142 powers to cancel RERA registration of Amrapali Group, ordering forensic audit and assigning stalled projects to NBCC to protect 42,000 homebuyers.

title: Universal Sompo General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Suresh Chand Jain
parties: Universal Sompo vs Suresh Chand Jain
summary: Clarified appellate hierarchy under the Consumer Protection Act 2019, discouraging High Courts from entertaining Article 226 petitions against NCDRC orders when statutory appeals exist.

title: Vodafone Idea Cellular Ltd. v. Ajay Kumar Agarwal
parties: Vodafone Idea vs Ajay Kumar Agarwal
summary: Held that consumer disputes against telecom service providers are maintainable before consumer forums despite Section 7B of the Indian Telegraph Act.

title: Fortune Infrastructure v. Trevor D'Lima
parties: Fortune Infrastructure vs Trevor D'Lima
summary: Held that a flat purchaser cannot be expected to wait indefinitely for possession; where builder fails to deliver within reasonable time, purchaser is entitled to full refund with compensation.

title: IREO Grace Realtech Pvt. Ltd. v. Abhishek Khanna
judge: D.Y. Chandrachud, Indu Malhotra, Indira Banerjee
parties: IREO Grace vs Abhishek Khanna
summary: Affirmed that remedies under the Consumer Protection Act and RERA are concurrent; flat buyers who received delayed occupancy certificates have right to elect appropriate forum.

title: Gurshinder Singh v. Shriram General Insurance Co. Ltd.
judge: U.U. Lalit, Indu Malhotra, Krishna Murari
parties: Gurshinder Singh vs Shriram General Insurance
summary: Held that if vehicle theft is reported to police immediately, mere delay in intimating the insurance company cannot be a ground to repudiate a genuine insurance claim.

title: Canara Bank v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
parties: Canara Bank vs United India Insurance
summary: Held that farmers who stored produce in a cold storage destroyed by fire are third-party beneficiaries entitled to recover directly under the insurance policy.

title: Secretary, Ministry of Defence v. Babita Puniya
parties: Secretary MoD vs Babita Puniya & Ors
summary: Landmark verdict directing the grant of Permanent Commission to Women Short Service Commission Officers in the Indian Army, striking down institutional gender barriers.

title: State of Uttarakhand v. Smt. Suman
judge: D.Y. Chandrachud, Indu Malhotra, Indira Banerjee
parties: State of Uttarakhand vs Smt. Suman
summary: Held that contractual female employees are entitled to full maternity benefits on equal footing with regular staff, in accordance with social justice under Article 42.

title: State of Punjab v. Jagjit Singh
parties: State of Punjab vs Jagjit Singh
summary: Held that temporary, daily-wage, and contractual employees performing identical duties as regular employees are entitled to minimum regular pay scale under 'equal pay for equal work'.

title: Lt. Col. Nitisha v. Union of India
parties: Lt. Col. Nitisha vs Union of India
summary: Formulated the legal framework for indirect discrimination under Indian constitutional law, holding that facially neutral evaluation benchmarks causing disproportionate impact violate Article 14.

title: Rajneesh Kumar v. Union of India
parties: Rajneesh Kumar vs Union of India
act_tags: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
summary: Reaffirmed reservation for persons with disabilities in public employment promotions, mandating reasonable accommodation as a facet of substantive equality.

title: National Car Rental v. All India Trade Union Congress
parties: Management vs Trade Union
summary: Interpreted the definition of 'workman' under Section 2(s) of Industrial Disputes Act, emphasizing the nature of primary duties rather than job designations.

title: State of Karnataka v. Umadevi (Re-affirmed)
judge: Y.K. Sabharwal, Arun Kumar, G.P. Mathur, C.K. Thakker, P.K. Balasubramanyan
parties: State of Karnataka vs Umadevi
summary: Constitution bench held that courts cannot direct absorption or regularization of temporary or ad-hoc public workers appointed without sanctioned recruitment process.

title: Jeetendra Kumar v. State of Rajasthan
parties: Jeetendra Kumar vs State of Rajasthan
summary: Reiterated that compassionate appointment is an exception to open recruitment aimed solely at relieving immediate financial distress, not an inheritable right.

title: Bharat Sanchar Nigam Ltd. v. Bhurumal
parties: BSNL vs Bhurumal
summary: Held that for brief service daily-wagers illegally retrenched under Section 25F, monetary compensation in lieu of reinstatement is the appropriate relief.

title: Union of India v. C. Girija
parties: Union of India vs C. Girija
summary: Held that mere inclusion of a candidate in a select list does not confer an indefeasible right to appointment if the employer decides for bona fide reasons not to fill vacancies.

title: Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab
judge: R.C. Lahoti, G.P. Mathur, P.K. Balasubramanyan
parties: Jacob Mathew vs State of Punjab
summary: Established that criminal prosecution of doctors under Section 304A IPC requires gross negligence or recklessness, substantiated by independent medical opinion.

title: Malay Kumar Ganguly v. Dr. Sukumar Mukherjee
parties: Malay Kumar Ganguly vs Dr. Sukumar Mukherjee
summary: Awarded unprecedented medical negligence damages, ruling that hospitals and consulting doctors are strictly liable for deviations from standard clinical treatment protocols.

title: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation
parties: Sarla Verma vs DTC
summary: Laid down the standardized multiplier method and dependency deduction formula for computing just compensation in motor accident fatal claim cases.

title: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi
judge: Dipak Misra, A.K. Sikri, A.M. Khanwilkar, D.Y. Chandrachud, Ashok Bhushan
parties: National Insurance Co. vs Pranay Sethi
summary: Five-judge constitution bench settled future prospects percentage additions (self-employed and salaried) and fixed compensation awards under conventional heads.

title: Mukund Dewangan v. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
judge: Amitava Roy, Arun Mishra, Sanjay Kishan Kaul
parties: Mukund Dewangan vs Oriental Insurance Co
summary: Held that a driver holding a Light Motor Vehicle (LMV) license is competent to drive a transport vehicle of unladen weight under 7,500 kg without separate endorsement.

title: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar
parties: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar
summary: Distinguished between medical physical impairment and functional disability affecting earning capacity, prescribing guidelines for assessment in injury claims.

title: Kirti v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd.
judge: N.V. Ramana, S. Abdul Nazeer, Surya Kant
parties: Kirti vs Oriental Insurance Co
summary: Recognized economic and emotional contribution of homemakers in accident claims, holding that calculation of notional income must account for their uncompensated domestic labor.

title: Kusum Sharma v. Batra Hospital & Medical Research Centre
parties: Kusum Sharma vs Batra Hospital
summary: Laid down comprehensive 11-point guidelines distinguishing between a bonafide clinical error of judgment and actionable medical negligence.

title: Biman Krishna Bose v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
parties: Biman Krishna Bose vs United India Insurance
summary: Held that public sector insurance companies cannot arbitrarily refuse to renew a medical insurance policy merely because previous claim disputes were raised.

title: Arun Kumar Agrawal v. National Insurance Co. Ltd.
parties: Arun Kumar Agrawal vs National Insurance
summary: Affirmed that the contribution of a deceased homemaker is invaluable and must be properly recognized in motor accident awards rather than dismissed on bare technicalities.
